title: EagleEye: Nanosatellite constellation design for high-coverage, high-resolution sensing
problem: Existing homogeneous satellite constellations cannot simultaneously achieve high coverage and high-resolution imaging—low-resolution cameras provide coverage but low image quality, while high-resolution cameras have limited geographic reach. Constellation design must respect strict timing constraints for multi-satellite coordination while completing target detection and scheduling within limited onboard computation time.
motivation: Satellite imagery enables valuable geospatial analysis applications including ship detection, environmental monitoring, and resource estimation, requiring constellation designs that maximize both coverage and resolution.
method: EagleEye uses a two-part system: a leader satellite with a low-resolution camera scans wide areas and detects targets onboard, then commands follower satellites with high-resolution cameras to photograph the detected targets. An optimization algorithm (integer linear programming, which finds the best assignment of satellites to targets) decides which followers should image which targets, ensuring camera movements complete quickly and all scheduling happens within strict time windows. This mixed-resolution approach lets each satellite specialize—the leader finds targets across a wide area, and followers provide high-quality images of those specific targets.
key_novelty: A mixed-resolution satellite constellation where a low-resolution leader detects targets and an optimization algorithm coordinates high-resolution followers to image them.
contributions: Mixed-resolution leader-follower constellation design for simultaneous high-coverage and high-resolution imaging
ILP-based scheduling algorithm for follower satellite target acquisition with actuation time constraints
Evaluation on four datasets showing 11-194% coverage improvement over existing solutions
